fact: 1916年1月《兵役法》通过（1月27日御准，3月2日生效），首次在英国本土实行义务兵役：18至41岁未婚男子及无子女鳏夫须服役，豁免医疗不合格者、神职人员、教师与部分保留职业；1916年5月的第二部《兵役法》把义务兵役扩大到已婚男子。爱尔兰不在该法适用范围内。

sources.title: UK Parliament, “Conscription: the First World War”
sources.quote: In January 1916 the Military Service Act was passed. This imposed conscription on all single men aged between 18 and 41, but exempted the medically unfit, clergymen, teachers and certain classes of industrial worker. ... A second Act passed in May 1916 extended conscription to married men.

sources.title: The National Archives, “MH 47/52/57 Central Military Service Tribunal”（馆藏说明）
sources.quote: On the 27 January 1916 the Military Service Act came into force in Great Britain, making every unmarried male aged between 18 and 41 (who was not in a reserved occupation) eligible for conscription into the armed forces. A second Act in May 1916 extended eligibility for military service to married men.

fact: 1916年11月16日，英国依《国防法》发布枢密院令，授权贸易委员会全面管制食品的进口、生产、分配、价格与质量；12月劳合·乔治联合政府依《新设部会法》设立食品部并任命德文波特勋爵为首任食品管制官（Food Controller），开始强制延长面粉出粉率、固定牛奶价格并限制公共餐饮的浪费。

sources.title: “Food Supply”（1922 年大英百科全书条目，Wikisource 转录）
sources.quote: The second step was the making of an Order in Council under the Defence of the Realm Act (Nov. 16) which practically empowered the Board of Trade to introduce a complete system of food control, by regulating the importation, production, distribution, prices and quality of all kinds of food or articles necessary for the production of food.

sources.title: “Food Supply”（1922 年大英百科全书条目，Wikisource 转录）
sources.quote: The new Coalition Government of Dec. 1916 included among its novelties a food controller to whom full powers were given under a “New Ministries Act.”

sources.title: Hancock, “The Social Impact of the First World War in Pembrokeshire”（Cardiff University 博士论文, 2015）
sources.quote: On 8 December 1916, Lord Devonport was appointed as the nation's first Food Controller.

fact: 1916年英国商船损失396艘，高于1915年的278艘、低于1917年的1,197艘；按对潜艇战果的统计，1916年英国口径为1,125艘、2,108,530总吨，德方口径为1,309艘、2,186,462总吨。单是1916年12月，英国商船即损失40艘、114,508吨。

sources.title: Maritime Archaeology Trust, “Forgotten Wrecks of the First World War: Overview”
sources.quote: British Merchant ship losses 1914: 64 British Merchant ship losses 1915: 278 British Merchant ship losses 1916: 396 British Merchant ship losses 1917: 1,197 British Merchant ship losses 1918: 544

sources.title: Maritime Archaeology Trust, “Forgotten Wrecks of the First World War: Overview”（引 Tarrant 与德方统计）
The Wreck of the Week, “War Diary: December 1916”
sources.quote: An official British source shows that 114,508 tons of British shipping were lost in December 1916 for 40 ships, while the overall total of mercantile shipping of all nationalities lost that month to all causes (mine, submarine torpedo, and surface ships) was 357,420 tons.

fact: 1916年10月10日英国贸易委员会主席朗西曼在下院报告：1914年7月至1916年9月，主要食品零售价平均上涨65%；把房租、衣着、燃料、照明等计入后，生活费上涨45%。以年度平均计，1916年食品价格比1914年7月高60%。

sources.title: Hansard, HC Written Answers, 10 October 1916, “Food Prices (Increase)”
sources.quote: The average increase in the retail prices of the principal articles of food between July, 1914, and September, 1916, was 65 per cent., assuming the continued consumption of the same commodities in the same proportions. In estimating the total change in cost of living, the rise in food prices should, of course, only be applied to the proportion of expenditure spent on food. Including, in addition, rent, clothing, fuel, light, and miscellaneous items of expenditure, the rise in cost of living during the War was found by the Food Prices Committee to be 45 per cent.

sources.title: Hansard, HC Written Answers, 15 November 1939, “Cost-of-Living Index”（历年平均值）
sources.quote: 1915 (average for year) 31 1916 (average for year) 60 1917 (average for year) 98½ 1918 (average for year) 115

fact: 1916年11月起英国强制提高面粉出粉率，从和平时期的76%提高到1917年2月的81%，并在面粉中掺入大麦、燕麦或黑麦粉，成品即深色的“战争面包”；面包本身始终未正式配给，而是靠控制面粉与价格维持供应。1917年4月起全部面粉厂被政府接管、按政府账目运行。

sources.title: The History Press, “Bread: A slice of First World War history”
sources.quote: The extraction rate rose from a peace-time level of 76 per cent in November 1916 to 81 per cent in February 1917, with admixtures of barley, oats or rye flour, and 92 per cent in March 1918, with added soya or potato flour. The bread was consequently dark in colour.

sources.title: “Food Supply”（1922 年大英百科全书条目，Wikisource 转录）
sources.quote: Food control actually began under this Order in Council, immediate steps being taken to lengthen compulsorily the extraction of flour (i.e. increase the proportion of the wheat berry which was made into flour, and so into human consumption, as against that which was left as “offals” to be used as feeding-stuffs for animals), to fix milk prices and to restrain extravagance in public meals.

sources.title: “Food Supply”（1922 年大英百科全书条目，Wikisource 转录）
sources.quote: To facilitate this the whole of the flour-mills were taken over and run on Government account as from April 1917.

fact: 《国防法》（DORA）在战时被修订扩展六次，授权政府征用土地建筑、设立新罪名并管制新闻、通信、饮酒与照明；1916年依该法体系新增的措施包括5月实行夏令时、规定制作白面粉与任老鼠侵入麦仓可处罚款，同年军事审查检查了30万封私人电报。违反条例可被逮捕、罚款、监禁甚至处死。

sources.title: The Gazette (UK Official Public Record), “World War 1: Defence of the Realm Act”
sources.quote: As the war progressed, as did DORA, being amended and extended six times over the course of the war (for example, Gazette supplement 29526).

sources.title: Imperial War Museums, “Surprising Laws Passed During The First World War”
sources.quote: British Summer Time was instituted in May 1916 to maximise working hours in the day, particularly in agriculture.

sources.title: Imperial War Museums, “Surprising Laws Passed During The First World War”
sources.quote: Military censors examined 300,000 private telegrams in 1916 alone.

fact: 1916年英国没有发行新的长期战争公债，全年战费靠四类短期“国库债券”（Exchequer Bonds）周转：1920年到期的5%债券募得2.05亿英镑；随后两笔5%债券（1919、1921年到期）共募1.74亿英镑，其中0.77亿是银行以旧债换新；1916年10月发行的6%债券三个月内募得1.61亿英镑。新的长期公债（第三次战争公债，5%按95英镑发行、实际收益率逾5.25%）直到1917年1月才推出。

sources.title: The Western Front Association, “The First World War paid off?”
sources.quote: The success of the Second War Loan meant that additional long term gilts did not need to be issued for about 18 months, and the cost of the war was financed through 1916 by the issue four classes of short term “Exchequer Bonds”.

sources.title: The Western Front Association, “The First World War paid off?”
sources.quote: A final Exchequer Bond was issue in October 1916, this offered interest at 6% and was scheduled for repayment in 1920. In just 3 months, this issue raised £161 million for the war effort.

sources.title: Hansard, HC, 26 February 1917, “Statement by Mr. Bonar Law”（第三次战争公债结果）
sources.quote: This makes a total of £1,000,312,950.

fact: 1916年9月15日英军在索姆河战役弗莱尔—库尔瑟莱特（Flers-Courcelette）首次把坦克投入战场：49辆Mark I奉命参战，当天只有32辆到达出发线，最终15至18辆进入无人区；多数因机械故障或陷入弹坑退出，英军当日推进约2,500码。Mark I为菱形车体、装甲约8毫米，可越过约2.7米宽的壕沟并碾过铁丝网，车内温度可达50°C。

sources.title: National Army Museum, “Attack of the tanks”
sources.quote: Forty-nine tanks of the Heavy Section would join the attack on the village of Flers-Courcellette on 15 September 1916. ... When the attack commenced only 15 out of 49 moved into no-mans land.

sources.title: The Tank Museum, “Tanks at Flers”
sources.quote: Forty-nine Mark I tanks were earmarked to take part, but on the day only thirty-two made it to the start line; the others having broken down or ditched. Eighteen eventually went into action, the rest suffered mechanical failure or became trapped in shell holes or trenches.

sources.title: The Tank Museum, “Tanks at Flers”
sources.quote: As a result of the day’s action the villages of Flers and Courcelette were captured, but the advance on 15 September was limited to about 2,500 yards (2.3km) on a three-mile front.

fact: 1916年是英国航运业利润的顶点：下院辩论引用的统计称，1916年航运净利约2.5亿英镑，而对2亿英镑资本的平均回报为67.5%，1913年同口径净利为2,000万英镑、回报10.5%；二手船价随之暴涨，1912年以17,000英镑购入的船在1916年卖到178,000英镑。该组数字出自议员引述《Statist》的估算，非官方审计账目。

sources.title: Hansard, HC, 17 July 1917, “Finance Bill”
sources.quote: The net profit for 1916, after paying all expenses except taxation—except Excess Profits Tax—the absolute net profit was no less a sum than £250,000,000 on a capital of £200,000,000.

sources.title: Hansard, HC, 17 July 1917, “Finance Bill”
sources.quote: What is the average dividend paid after Excess Profits Tax has been paid? The average interest on the £200,000,000 capital in 1916 was 67½ per cent., as against 10½ per cent. in the year before the War, 1913. ... the net profits for 1913 were £20,000,000 and the net profits for 1916 were £250,000,000.

sources.title: Hansard, HC, 16 March 1920, “Supply 10th March”（船舶转售案例）
sources.quote: One, which was purchased in 1905 for £26,000, was sold in 1915 for £145,000. Another, bought m 1912 for £17,000, was sold in 1916 for £178,000.
